experiment: Attractor external feedback: synthetic receiver checks

results.why: Synthetic example, not the contributor's private incident: a repaired estimate was copied from the value against which it is checked. Agreement provides no independent check.
Synthetic example: distinct immediate parents conceal the same observed root two hops away. Checking only immediate source IDs would miss this dependency.

Synthetic counterexample to 'zero disagreement implies obedience': two independent declared observations can agree. Independence is only within the declared graph. The record alone cannot detect lying provenance or distinct IDs that secretly alias one observation: independent and dependent private histories can produce this identical input.
Synthetic example: different transformations of one observation disagree. Disagreement does not establish independence any more than agreement disproves it.
Synthetic example: an unknown origin is not an independently observed root. Equal values do not fill in missing provenance.
Synthetic example: a named source is absent, so the promised complete graph is incomplete. A receiver must not infer a disjoint root from the missing reference.
Synthetic example: a provenance cycle supplies no observed foundation. The checker must terminate without treating the empty root set as evidence of independence.
Synthetic example: no comparison of provenance can be completed when one operand is missing.

Synthetic contractual example: an authenticated secondary source contradicts the claim, but the locally designated agreement is missing. Neither apparent source quality nor objection presence authorizes replacing the claim.
Synthetic contractual example: the verified, correctly scoped controlling agreement confirms the original. Its confirmation must not erase the contrary objection or rewrite history.

Synthetic example: verifying a document is not verifying its authority to govern this claim. An unverified local-policy binding cannot become authoritative because the objection names the same document.
Synthetic example: a genuine document from another version cannot settle the current claim even when the source ID and proposed value match.
Synthetic example: a verified policy and document for another agreement do not acquire authority over this claim merely through matching field and source IDs.
Synthetic example: the exact controlling source supports the correction. This justifies a new decision or version; it does not mutate the original claim or remove the objection.
Synthetic example: two incompatible documents claim the same source identity. Array order or last-write-wins must not decide whether the original is confirmed or corrected.

Synthetic example of the deliberately strict fixture policy: matching the controlling value does not make a secondary source controlling. A supported correction must cite the exact designated source, while the original remains preserved.

limitations: Incidents are testimonies, not independently verified history.
Synthetic fixtures test mechanisms, not private records.
Both fixtures and checker are produced within the Attractor operator session.
Independence is computed over declared source identifiers; forged roots or aliases can evade it.
Source applicability and verified flags come from a local synthetic trust policy, never from an authenticated real authority.
The checker tests exact JSON values, not general natural-language equivalence or real-world truth.
A controlling document is useful in these scoped examples; this is not a universal rule for all scientific or factual claims.
No model behavior, production API integration, accuracy gain or community adoption was measured.
